title: Communications Legislation Amendment (SBS Advertising Flexibility) Bill 2017
short_title: Communications Legislation Amendment (SBS Advertising Flexibility) Bill 2017

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would give the Special Broadcasting Service (SBS) more flexibility to schedule advertising and sponsorship announcements, and expressly permit revenue from product placement.
It would raise the hourly advertising and sponsorship limit from five to 10 minutes while adding a cap of 120 minutes in any 24 hours.
The changes would start the day after Royal Assent, with existing rules on advertising around programs and during natural breaks continuing to apply.
changes: SBS would be expressly authorised to earn money from paid product placement.
The board would have to develop and publish guidelines governing product placement.
Annual reports would disclose product placement revenue and identify paying advertisers or sponsors.
summary.affected: SBS and its board, and viewers who may see more advertising per hour at some times and less at others, are affected.

speeches.speaker: Paul Fletcher
speeches.brief: The bill amends the SBS Act to allow up to 10 minutes of advertising per hour (capped at 120 minutes daily) and clarify rules for product placement, projected to raise $27.4 million over four years. The changes aim to increase SBS's commercial revenue and reduce its reliance on government funding without materially affecting commercial broadcasters.

speeches.speaker: Paul Fletcher
speeches.brief: The government decided not to proceed with the SBS Advertising Flexibility Bill, and instead provided SBS with an additional $8.8 million in the 2017‑18 budget, bringing total investment to over $280 million for that year.
